title: Total, average and sum through primitive streams

blocks.text: `mapToInt`, `mapToLong` and `mapToDouble` move from a `Stream<T>` to a primitive stream, which brings `sum()` and `average()` with it and avoids boxing every number. `IntStream.average()` returns an `OptionalDouble`, because an empty stream has no average.

items: `totalLength(List<String> words)` returns the sum of the words' lengths.

`average(List<String> numbers)` parses each string as an `int` (`Integer.parseInt`, so `"2.5"` throws `NumberFormatException`) and returns the exact average as an `OptionalDouble`, even for values near `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.
`sum(List<Integer> values)` returns the sum of the values as a `long`.

blocks.text: Choose the primitive stream that can hold the answer, and let "no numbers" stay visible to the caller.

cases.says: It totals the lengths, averages the parsed numbers and sums the values.
An empty list has no average: the answer is an empty OptionalDouble, not 0.0.
Sums and averages of large values are exact: the sum is taken over a LongStream, and the average of two Integer.MAX_VALUE values is Integer.MAX_VALUE.

concepts: mapToInt, mapToLong and mapToDouble move to a primitive stream with sum() and average() and no boxing.
